newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline ends higher on supply concerns.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline ends higher on supply concerns.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline ended higher Thursday on concerns of tightening supplies generated by refinery problems, and views a push to replenish low distillate stocks will come at the expense of gasoline output.
"I think a major effort is a afoot to boost distillate stocks, and given the high production of distillate, the fear is that gasoline will suffer," said Steve Platt, an analyst with Dean Witter.
November gasoline ended up 1.06 cent a gallon to 69.22 cents, while November heating oil settled 0.47 cent lower at 70.49 cents a gallon.
Prospects of larger total distillate supply, which includes heating oil, weighed on heating oil prices. December crude followed heating oil lower, settling off 35 cents a barrel to $24.51.

After heating oil stocks hit historically low levels, mounting political pressure to replenish stocks ahead of winter has driven distillate production to a record high of 3.7 million barrels a day, traders said.
Also, Colonial Pipeline Co has said it would make room on its gasoline line to accomodate a surge in requests to ship distillates on its huge pipeline.

Meanhwile, there was talk that large refiners were buying gasoline in the cash market, indicating that their refinery operations are not generating enough gasoline, since output is skewed toward distillates, traders said.

"The big thing today was that Exxon, Chevron and Texaco (Star Enterprise) were seen in the cash market. These guys have been maxing out on heat, so the need for gasoline must be there," said a trader.
Gasoline prices continued to receive a boost from a partial outage at Petroleos de Venezuela's huge (PDVSA) Amuay refinery, a large gasoline maker, traders said.
A 108,000 barrel a day catalytic cracker went down due to problems with an air compressor, and PDVSA officials expect the problem to take three weeks to fix.
Venezuela is the largest exporter of gasoline to the United States, and Amuay is said to supply as many as 60,000 barrels per day to U.S. gasoline markets.
Talk that refiners were looking to buy gasoline in the cash markets sparked rumors they were also suffering outages.

Exxon said it was not having problems with its large Baytown refinery in Texas. Company officials for the refineries could not be immediately reached, but environmental regulators said they did not know of these refinery problems, either in Texas or Louisiana.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
